question.problem:
For which of the following situations can the distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where $p$ is the population proportion?

I. A sample of size $n=100$ from a population of size $N=500$ in which $90%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.

II. A sample of size $n=60$ from a population of size $N=1\,500$ in which $90%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.

III. A sample of size $n=40$ from a population of size $N=1\,500$ in which $90%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where 

- $n\le 5%\cdot N$ (the sample size is less than (or equal to) $5%$ of the population size),

- $np>5$ (more than $5$ sample elements have the characteristic), and

- $n(1-p)>5$ (more than $5$ sample elements do not have the characteristic).

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =100, \\ 5%\cdot N & =0.05\cdot 500 \\  & =25 \\  & <100.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Since  the sample size is more than $5%$ of the population size, we *cannot* approximate the distribution of $\overset{^}{\,p}$ using the given model.

- In situation II, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =60 \\  & \le 5%\cdot N \\  & =0.05\cdot 1\,500 \\  & =75\,✓ \\ np & =60(0.90) \\  & =54 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =60(1-0.90) \\  & =6 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can approximate the distribution of $\overset{^}{\,p}$ using the given model.

- In situation III, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =40 \\  & \le 5%\cdot N \\  & =0.05\cdot 1\,500 \\  & =75\,✓ \\ np & =40(0.9) \\  & =36 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =40(1-0.9) \\  & =4 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Since $n(1-p)≯5,$ we *cannot* approximate the distribution of $\overset{^}{\,p}$ using the given model.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
